name: Immer
overview: Immer was a male Levite priest who held the distinguished position as the sixteenth priest chosen among the twenty-four priestly courses. He belonged to the line of Ithamar, one of the two sons of Aaron, which situates him within a specific priestly lineage. This identification highlights his role within the organized service of the temple as recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:14.
namesAndTitles: The name Immer means "lamb," a proper name not given directly by God. This name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:14 and reflects a common practice of Hebrew names carrying symbolic or everyday meanings without necessarily indicating divine origin.
familyAndRelationships: Immer is identified as a descendant of Ithamar, linking him to one of Aaron's sons and thus to the priestly lineage. Additionally, he is inferred to be an ancestor of Pashhur, as noted in Jeremiah 20:1. These relationships situate Immer within a recognized priestly family line important in biblical history.
scriptureSignificance: Immer's significance lies in his role within the structured priestly courses established for temple service, emphasizing the organized worship system in ancient Israel. His placement as the sixteenth priestly course in the line of Ithamar reflects the division of priestly duties and the continuity of priestly responsibilities through generations. This organization underlines the importance of maintaining order and heritage in the Levitical priesthood.
